industry: Residential garage door sales, installation, spring/opener repair, and preventive tune-ups
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Licensed' / 'C-13' / 'bonded/insured' if not currently true in the service state
Invented hail/storm 'your neighborhood was hit' without a factual basis
'Lifetimeproof' / 'maintenance-free forever' / lifetime claims that exceed the real warranty
Manufacturer warranty stated as if it were the contractor's labor warranty without distinction
APR-free '0% financing' without term, fees, and approved-credit conditions when required
DIY spring tips that encourage unsafe consumer spring work while selling fear
'From $99 springs' bait if most jobs are far higher — use 'starting at' only with clear scope
compliance_notes: State contractor licensing: garage door installation/repair often requires a contractor license (classification varies; California example via CSLB). Do not advertise as a licensed contractor if unlicensed. Verify the client's license class before printing.
FTC s.5 / 16 CFR 233/251: dollar-off, percent-off, free estimates, free remotes — bona fide prices and conditions.

Financing ads: if a rate, monthly payment, or '0%' is stated, include required credit disclosures (TILA/Reg Z concepts; state retail-installment/open-end ad rules e.g. CA B&P 17538.7 patterns) — 'financing available' alone is safer than a naked rate.
Warranty clarity: separate manufacturer product warranty from installer labor warranty in copy.
Safety claims about springs/cables: do not overclaim injury statistics you cannot source; do encourage professional service consistent with industry safety guidance.
Storm/hurricane ratings: only claim tested ratings the product actually carries; no fake storm-damage urgency.
39 USC 3001: no official inspection notice look-alikes.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, relief, status, belonging are fine when they fit and stay legal.
Every angle and emotion_by_offer combo carries sell_the_outcome_line.
Vendor ROI labeled agency-only unverified; never print as fact on a client card.
Prefer one clear offer + one real photo + one QR (roofing-round5 directional) unless client insists on a coupon grid.
No age/senior default unless the client has a real discount and evidence supports targeting.
